kurals.tr: Kaimmaaru Ventaa Katappaatu Maarimaattu / En Aatrung Kollo Ulaku
kurals.m: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?

kurals.tr: Thaalaatrith Thandha Porulellaam Thakkaarkku / Velaanmai Seydhar Poruttu
kurals.m: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence

kurals.tr: Puththe Lulakaththum Eentum Peralaridhe / Oppuravin Nalla Pira
kurals.m: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods

kurals.tr: Oththa Tharavon Uyirvaazhvaan Matraiyaan / Seththaarul Vaikkap Patum
kurals.m: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence) He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead

kurals.tr: Ooruni Neernirain Thatre Ulakavaam / Perari Vaalan Thiru
kurals.m: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank

kurals.tr: Payanmaram Ulloorp Pazhuththatraal Selvam / Nayanutai Yaankan Patin
kurals.m: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town

kurals.tr: Marundhaakith Thappaa Maraththatraal Selvam / Perundhakai Yaankan Patin
kurals.m: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease

kurals.tr: Itanil Paruvaththum Oppuravirku Olkaar / Katanari Kaatchi Yavar
kurals.m: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth

kurals.tr: Nayanutaiyaan Nalkoorndhaa Naadhal Seyumneera / Seyyaadhu Amaikalaa Vaaru
kurals.m: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same

kurals.tr: Oppuravi Naalvarum Ketenin Aqdhoruvan / Vitrukkol Thakka Thutaiththu
kurals.m: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self
